A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with AWEDIST renamed Token Distillation in v2. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original biomedical benchmark evaluations, biomedical and multi-word definition-generation results, ablations, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds FrenchBench evaluations and original comparisons with Tokens to Words.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same frozen-model procedure, aligned hidden-state MSE objective, context retrieval/generation, joint optimization of new embeddings, and optional NTP combinations with automatic loss scaling. The method and baseline renamings do not change these procedures.

E1.justification: v2 adds French language adaptation using FineWeb-2 contexts and eight FrenchBench multiple-choice tasks covering vocabulary, grammar, inference, and question answering/reading comprehension. This substantially extends coverage beyond v1's biomedical and multi-word definition evaluations, which remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds Tokens to Words (Kaplan et al., 2025) to the biomedical comparison and evaluates it on FrenchBench in Appendix A.1, Tables 8–9. Existing comparators remain: v1's NTP++ becomes NTP, while its original NTP becomes NTP (tune all embeddings).

E3.justification: The retained biomedical protocols are unchanged. New French experiments specify five-shot evaluation with letter answer choices and include Qwen3-8B-Base. The added Tokens to Words comparison introduces a distinct control limitation: tokens with failed PatchScopes extractions are omitted from its expanded vocabulary.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1 adds an extraction-failure analysis for Tokens to Words, reporting failures for approximately 10–40% of biomedical tokens and 50–75% of French tokens. Existing objective, initialization, context-source, target-layer, joint-versus-isolated optimization, and two-epoch analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both retain the stated five-seed policy, biomedical mean/standard-deviation reporting, Bonferroni-corrected one-sided Welch tests, specified single-seed ablations, and minimum runtime over three runs. No changed repetition count or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is stated.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial FrenchBench results: Table 3 reports averages of 72.9 for Token Distillation, 70.8 for NTP, and 73.2 for original tokenization. Tables 8–9 add Tokens to Words results under its partial-vocabulary setting. Retained biomedical, definition-generation, ablation, and runtime values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same tokenizer and hidden-state definitions, mapped-position condition, and optimization objective. Expanding the denominator notation from |M| to |M(sτ,sτ⋆)| and removing the loss-name prefix are equivalent notation changes; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: distilling Transformer representations produces high-quality new input embeddings and outperforms aggregation, NTP training, and pretrained hypernetwork baselines. French evaluation supplies additional support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 discusses hypernetwork language-distribution mismatch and explains how Tokens to Words' partial token coverage can inflate its comparative scores. It also qualifies the unseen-language limitation and adds an explanation that tokenization speedups for fixed input text are independent of embedding quality. Most existing limitations are simply relocated.

D1.justification: v2 documents French token selection and evaluation commands, identifies the Qwen checkpoint, and supplies 100-token biomedical and French examples. Existing optimizer, hardware, prompts, and runtime details remain. The code/lock-file disclosure changes from available to future availability, although the first-page code footnote still says available.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of Tokens to Words/PatchScopes and concurrent distillation-trained hypernetworks, alongside newer tokenization, adaptation, FrenchBench, and Qwen references. Gururangan et al. (2020) is removed. The existing distinction between model-gradient-free and gradient-based initialization remains the organizing framework.

P1.justification: v2 renames the paper, method, and NTP variants, edits introductory explanations, and adds ELLIS affiliations. Limitations move into the main text, and appendix results/runtime sections are reorganized, while most prose and the main section sequence remain. Renaming leaves an ambiguous 'NTP outperforms NTP' sentence in Section 5.1.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the document and tables, replacing most diagonal model headers with horizontal headers and revising typography, captions, and placement. It adds FrenchBench Table 3 and appendix Tables 8–9, which redisplay comparisons with Tokens to Words. Figure 3 is relocated; existing plotted results remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: FrenchBench provides evidence for language adaptation that v1 lacked, while the Tokens to Words comparison addresses a closely related alternative and explicitly discloses its extraction failures. Added implementation examples and applicability discussion improve transparency. These are useful incremental gains: the core evidence remains unchanged, and unequal token coverage limits the strength of the new comparator evaluation.
